items.q: Fill up: The HUS triad is thrombocytopenia, renal failure and ______.
items.exp: Triad: thrombocytopenia, renal failure, microangiopathic hemolytic anemia (MAHA). (Book p753)

items.q: All of the following form the HUS triad EXCEPT:
items.exp: Fever belongs to the TTP pentad, not the HUS triad. (Book p753)

items.q: Compared with the HUS triad, the TTP pentad adds fever, GI symptoms and:
items.exp: TTP pentad: thrombocytopenia, fever, MAHA, neurological symptoms [brain], GI symptoms. (Book p753)

items.q: Which statement comparing the two shapes is TRUE?
opts: The HUS triangle is thrombocytopenia, renal failure and MAHA, while TTP's pentagon adds fever, GI and neurological symptoms
The HUS triangle includes fever while TTP's pentagon does not
TTP's pentagon replaces renal failure with neurological symptoms
Both shapes list exactly the same five features
items.exp: Triad vs pentagon as drawn: TTP adds GI symptoms, fever and neurological symptoms [brain]. (Book p753)

items.q: Typical HUS/D+ begins in childhood, commonly below the age of:
items.exp: Typical HUS/D+ onset: childhood, commonly age <5 years; cause: infection i.e dysentery; prognosis good. (Book p753)

items.q: Atypical HUS/D- differs from typical HUS by:
opts: Any-age onset, genetic (m/c) or sporadic drug-induced cause, and 50% progressing to ESRD with post-transplant recurrence
Childhood onset with dysentery and a good prognosis
items.exp: Atypical HUS/D-: any age; genetic (m/c)/sporadic (drug induced); bad prognosis (50% progress to ESRD); ↑ recurrence after renal transplant. (Book p753)
